source.title: Discovering Event Structure in Continuous Narrative Perception and Memory

confidence_rationale: Supports the COORDINATION half of Q-095 specifically -- that segmentation, encoding and retrieval are one pipeline rather than three independently-registered mechanisms -- which is the part of the question that the other entries in this directory address least. High-order event boundaries are coupled to hippocampal activity, and that hippocampal response PREDICTS pattern reinstatement during later free recall: the segmenter's output is what determines what is retrievable, which is the reciprocal coupling MECH-495 proposes and MECH-288 would have to implement. Confidence is held to 0.64 because the evidence is correlational naturalistic fMRI with no model comparison -- the paper never contrasts a segmentation-based account against a continuous trajectory-memory account, so it establishes that the coupling exists without establishing that it adds capability over the alternative, which is precisely what Q-095 asks.
failure_signatures: An REE segmenter whose boundaries do not influence what is subsequently retrievable is not participating in a coordinated organising principle -- it is a boundary detector whose output nothing consumes, and MECH-288 being 'built' does not by itself discharge this.

Event structure is NESTED and timescale-graded (short events in sensory regions, long events in high-order areas). A single-timescale segmenter cannot reproduce this, and a Q-095 test that fixes one segmentation granularity may fail for a reason unrelated to the question.

Anticipatory reinstatement on a familiar narrative is a positive signature: a coordinated system should pre-activate the upcoming event representation before its boundary arrives. Absence of anticipation in REE would indicate retrieval is reactive rather than organised.

mapping.source_claim_statement: During continuous naturalistic perception, cortical activity is structured into a nested hierarchy of discrete events -- short in sensory regions, long in high-order areas representing abstract multimodal situation models. Boundaries between high-order events are coupled to increases in hippocampal activity, and that hippocampal response predicts pattern reinstatement during later free recall; familiar narratives additionally show anticipatory reinstatement.
mapping.ree_translation: The coordination Q-095 asks about is empirically visible as a chain: segmentation determines boundary, boundary drives hippocampal encoding, encoding determines what is later retrievable. In REE terms, MECH-288's segmenter output should be causally upstream of what ContextMemory stores and therefore of what can be completed later. This is the reciprocal coupling MECH-495 proposes (persistent context mismatch raises separation / opens an episode; successful completion supports persistence), observed rather than assumed. It also constrains any Q-095 test design: segmentation is nested and timescale-graded, so an ablation at a single fixed granularity tests one rung of a ladder, not the principle.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is correlational naturalistic fMRI with no model comparison. The paper shows that a segmentation-coupled encoding pipeline EXISTS in humans; it does not show that a system with one outperforms a system without one, because no such contrast was run. Q-095 asks the comparative question, so this entry constrains the shape of a good test far more than it moves the verdict. The event-detection method is itself a model fitted to the data (a HMM-style stable-pattern-shift detector), so 'discovered' boundaries are boundaries under that model's assumptions.
mapping.source_context: Human fMRI during continuous audiovisual narrative (movie and spoken story) perception, plus free recall; data-driven boundary detection without stimulus annotation.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron, open access, methodologically influential and widely replicated in the naturalistic-imaging literature; the data-driven boundary detection is a genuine methodological contribution rather than annotation-following. Mapping fidelity is the limiter: the paper is about the existence and coupling of the pipeline, while Q-095 is a comparative capability question the paper does not pose. Transfer risk covers human-narrative-to-agent-episode plus the dependence of 'event' on the fitted detection model.
